As I just posted on the topic of making homemade black powder for my Model of 1873 Trap Door Springfield, I would like to point out that the old black powdered cartridges were not that bad, and many states you don't need background check to purchase one. There were 700,000 of them made so you should be able to find one. They are accurate and because of the very heavy bullet they are deadly out to about 500 yards with the trajectory of an howitzer. My 1873 holds 2 inch groups at a 100 yards all day long. (Tip clean he bore every 10 or so rounds as the powder fouling causes the velocity and pressure to creep up causing less drop.)

I take issue with the author of the article about using pre 1899 weapons. These were made with old metallurgy technology and designed for black powder so they may not handle the pressures of today's ammunition. Remember the pre 800,000 M1903 Springfield bolt actions had some concern about improper heat treating that may cause catastrophic failure, (though there has not been any proof of a failure as far as I know).
